**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 00:06
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The VIDAS Nephrocheck is a diagnostic tool designed to assist in the early detection of acute kidney injury (AKI) in critically ill patients.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The VIDAS Nephrocheck works in conjunction with the VIDAS 3 to test for the protein biomarkers IGFBP7 and TIMP2 in order to calculate the approximate AKI risk score in patients with acute cardiovascular and/or respiratory compromise.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The system consists of NEPH Reagent Strips, NEPH Solid Phase Receptacles (SPR), and a NEPH control and calibrator.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The VIDAS Nephrocheck principle combines an enzyme immunoassay competition method with a final fluorescent detection (ELFA).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The interior of the NEPH SPR is coated with mouse monoclonal IgG anti‑IGFBP‑7 and anti‑TIMP‑2, serving as both the solid phase and pipetting device for the assay.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The system is designed to automatically perform all assay steps, providing quick and reliable results.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The VIDAS Nephrocheck is intended to identify high-risk patients within 12 hours of assessment, allowing for the implementation of early renal-protective actions to reduce AKI frequency and severity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The system is designed to rule out patients with confidence, adapt treatment using goal-directed protocols, and help healthcare professionals make informed decisions about patient care.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Reagent Strips consist of 10 wells covered with a labeled foil seal, with six wells containing conjugate, wash buffers, and substrate, and the last well containing the fluorescence substrate.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] This system is intended for use in the clinical evaluation of patients, with NEPH liquid controls and calibration verification kits sold separately.
